page: Microsoft Azure M128-64bds_3_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8473C processor running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. Configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs across 32 physical cores at 4.0 GHz, the architecture incorporates 105 MB of L3 cache alongside advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for int8 and bfloat16 data types. The instance lacks dedicated GPU hardware but includes 6442 GB of high-speed local solid-state drive (SSD) storage.

A primary architectural characteristic of this server is its substantial memory capacity of 2794.0 GB, delivering roughly 43.66 GB of RAM per vCPU. This configuration translates to top-tier benchmark throughput, exhibiting uncached large-block read speeds of 367.66 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 169.25 GB/sec. Parallel processing capacity is substantiated by a Geekbench multi-core score of 20113.0, a multi-core stress-ng metric of 67529.51, and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 413.66 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance scored 35100.58 in PassMark tests, complementing a throughput of 87.35 million Redis SET operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the M128-64bds_3_v3 represents an enterprise-tier profile designed to minimize cluster node counts by consolidating enormous memory-footprint workloads onto a single host. The balance between 64 compute threads, extensive bundled local SSD space, and high uncached memory bandwidth prevents bottlenecks typical of large-scale distributed memory architectures, though single-core compute performance remains in the median bracket compared to pure compute-optimized families.

The hardware configuration makes the M128-64bds_3_v3 suitable for large-scale in-memory databases such as SAP HANA, massive Redis caching layers, memory-resident data analytics, and real-time enterprise transaction processing systems.
